title: Fuzzy contact linkage probe log
content:
Purpose: quick, informal log of experiments and human-labeler guidance for linking user/contact records when identifiers are missing or noisy. Goal is pragmatic rules that labelers can apply consistently and that we can codify later into automated scoring heuristics.

Background/context:
- We have ~22M contact rows from product telemetry + onboarding CSVs. Many duplicates because of name variants, different emails, mobile numbers with country code/no-code, and legacy CRM imports.
- Downstream features (recommendations, SSO linking, customer support views) break if we over-merge; we prefer conservative linking with an abstain option.
- Current automated dedupe removes exact email/phone matches, but misses nickname variants and international formatting.

Notes to self (labeler-friendly rules, working draft):
1) High-confidence link (label: LINK): any one of:
   - exact match on verified email (user-verified at signup) OR
   - exact match on phone number after E.164 normalization AND at least one matching name token (first or last) OR
   - exact match on internal customer_id
   Implementation note: mark as LINK and capture reason.

2) Probable link (label: PROBABLE_LINK): any of:
   - fuzzy name match (Jaro-Winkler >= 0.92) AND emails differ but one email is a known alias (gmail dots/plus)
   - same phone after normalization but different country code present and other metadata (zip, company) matches
   - same company domain email and names look like variants (e.g., "Jon Smith" vs "Jonathan Smith")
   Labeler guidance: use PROBABLE_LINK if you would manually merge in CRM but are unsure. Leave a short rationale.

3) Possible link (label: POSSIBLE_LINK — requires review or multiple records aggregated):
   - same last name + overlapping freeform address fragments ("415 Market" vs "415 Market St")
   - similar mobile numbers with transposed digits (one off) and same signup IP range
   Use only when additional evidence exists; mark for adjudication batch.

4) NOT_LINK:
   - same full name but different verified email domains and conflicting company names
   - same phone area code but different country and mismatched timezone/activity
   - records that look like shared household contacts (spouse, parent) where merging would lose separate identities

5) ABSTAIN: when uncertain (e.g., name + generic email like info@ or firstname.lastname@ but no vetting) — mark ABSTAIN and add short note "insufficient evidence". These should be routed to adjudication.

Examples (include in labeling UI as quick snippets):
- Example A: "A. Chen" (phone +1 415-555-0123, email a.chen+work@gmail.com) and "Angela Chen" (phone 4155550123, email angela.chen@gmail.com) => LINK (phone normalized exact, email is alias).
- Example B: "Mike O'Conner" (mike@acme.com) and "Michael Oconnor" (m.oconnor@acme.co) => PROBABLE_LINK (name variant + same company domain, domain difference flagged).
- Example C: "Sara Li" (sli@mail.com) and "Sara Li" (sli+promo@mail.com) but different IPs and signup months 2y apart => PROBABLE_LINK if activity patterns overlap, else ABSTAIN.

Labeler heuristics and micro-guidance (common edgecases):
- Gmail variants: treat dots and plus suffixes as same local address, but still check sign-up verification metadata. If both verified long ago, lean LINK.
- Corporate forwarding aliases: when an email is forwarded (e.g., name@partners.acme.com -> name@acme.com) we often see different recorded addresses; prefer PROBABLE_LINK unless phone or verification present.
- Hyphenated names: treat hyphens optional in token compare.
- Non-latin scripts: if transliterated names match high-confidence fuzzy threshold and at least one contact point matches, allow PROBABLE_LINK. If uncertain, ABSTAIN and tag for bilingual adjudicator.

Operational instructions for label queues:
- Priority 1: records with high downstream impact (billing accounts, enterprise admin contacts) — labelers must use conservative rules; escalate PROBABLE_LINK to product owner for rollback policy.
- Priority 2: general user dedupe. Use ABSTAIN threshold higher (i.e., be more conservative).
- Provide adjudication notes: short bullet of evidence and algorithmic signals (score values, matched tokens).

Metrics to capture during pilot:
- Precision of LINK (manual audit sample of 1k merges after applying labels) — target >= 99% for LINK merges.
- Recall improvement over exact-match baseline for recoverable duplicates — target +18% duplicates identified by humans but missed by baseline.
- Volume of ABSTAINS per 10k candidate pairs — helps size adjudication team.

Small experiments to run (quick):
- Run Jaro-Winkler name threshold sweep from 0.88 to 0.96 and sample labeler agreement at each point.
- Compare phone normalization libs (libphonenumber vs in-house) on edge cases (extensions, intl variations).
- Alias expansion: apply gmail dot/plus normalization and check how many records become LINK vs PROBABLE.

Open questions / discussion points for Evan & Priya:
- How to handle shared devices (same phone seen across household)? Should we tie to activity patterns or opt for ABSTAIN?
- Can we include login/verification timestamps as a required strong signal for LINK? (pros: reduces false merges; cons: old verified accounts lose linking)
- Is there appetite to build a lightweight adjudication UI that shows top 5 evidence points and allows single-click merge + rollback?

TODO (short actionable items):
- [ ] Create 500-sample audit set of LINK labels for precision check (me + Evan) — ETA 2025-12-10
- [ ] Implement email alias normalization pipeline for labeling UI (Priya) — ETA 2025-11-30
- [ ] Sweep Jaro thresholds and log labeler agreement (automation task) — owner: Maya
- [ ] Draft adjudication quickscript for batch review (show diffs, allow decision tagging) — owner: Evan

Random notes / heuristics stash (for future formalization):
- When last names are common ("Lee", "Smith"), require at least two non-name evidence signals for PROBABLE_LINK.
- For records created within 24h of each other with same IP and similar name -> lean LINK.
- If one record has an SSO_identity_id and the other doesn't -> require matching phone/email or ABSTAIN.

Scratch ideas for ML features (for later):
- name_similarity_score, normalized_email_local, phone_e164, signup_ip_cluster_id, company_domain_similarity, activity_overlap_days, last_active_gap_days, verification_age_days
- quick model to propose merge probability then have labeler confirm for borderline cases.

End of note. Save as working reference. When we move to formal guideline, break into: 1) labeler quick reference sheet, 2) automated heuristic codebook, 3) adjudication UI requirements.
